factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Expenses section: Electricity costs increased by EUR 0.7 million (+28.8%) to EUR 3,096 thousand (3.096 million). Technical maintenance and repair increased by EUR 1.2 million (+80.0%) to EUR 2,784 thousand (2.784 million).

factual_claims.claim: The latter increase reflected more extensive repairs to Botnica, ferries and harbour infrastructure, while the previous year included a EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity for Botnica repairs.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Expenses section: Technical maintenance increase reflects more extensive repair works on Botnica, ferries, and harbour infrastructure. Note 12*: EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity received in 2025 for Botnica repairs.

factual_claims.claim: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased 6.0% to EUR 12.9 million, partly due to the commissioning of a new quay and capitalised ferry dry-docking projects.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased by EUR 0.7 million (+6.0%) to EUR 12,867 thousand (12.867 million). Reason includes commissioning of new quay and capitalised ferry dry-docking projects.

factual_claims.claim: Operating volumes weakened: cargo declined 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, mainly because liquid bulk fell 33.8%, while passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million and vessel calls fell 4.8%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section: Cargo volume 6,481 thousand tonnes (6.5 million) vs 6,825 (2025) = -5.0%. Liquid bulk down 33.8%. Passengers 3,586 thousand (3.586 million) vs 3,659 (2025) = -2.0%. Vessel calls 3,376 vs 3,546 = -4.8%.

factual_claims.claim: Helsinki passenger traffic was affected by the scheduled dry-docking of Eckerö Line’s Finlandia.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Passenger volumes section: Largest decline on Tallinn-Helsinki route due to scheduled dry-docking of Eckerö Line’s vessel Finlandia at beginning of year.

factual_claims.claim: The report also links lower liquid-bulk volumes and higher fuel costs to geopolitical conditions, including Russia’s war in Ukraine and the US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Main Economic Risks section: Instability from US-Iran conflict and Russia’s military activity in Ukraine increased fuel costs and affected liquid bulk volumes.

factual_claims.claim: The comparison was further weakened by EUR 0.9 million of profit from the 2025 Rail Baltica land sale and other prior-year benefits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report: Result for comparative period positively affected by profit from disposal of land for Rail Baltica project and insurance indemnity. Operating Expenses section notes absence of insurance indemnity and one-off profit from land sale in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Lower net finance costs, down 11.2% to EUR 2.3 million, partly mitigated the operating decline.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Finance Costs section: Net finance costs decreased by EUR 0.3 million (–11.2%) to EUR 2,279 thousand (2.279 million). Candidate rounding to 2.3 million acceptable.

factual_claims.claim: The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, resulting in a EUR 4.4 million reduction in cash to EUR 27.6 million and operating cash flow of EUR 18.2 million, down from EUR 26.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Dividends section: EUR 19.2 million dividend paid. Cash Flow Statement: Cash and cash equivalents at 30 June 2026: 27,616 thousand (27.616 million) vs 31,993 (beginning). Operating cash flow 18,151 thousand (18.151 million) vs 26,293 (2025).
